title.narrative: Linking Agriculture, Natural Resource Management and Nutrition (LANN)

description.narrative: Despite government efforts to improve nutrition in Sierra Leone, high rates of undernutrition and malnutrition persist. In an extension to a previous project, Welthungerhilfe is providing further training to established women's groups in villages, educating them on topics such as healthy eating and better hygiene. This combination was chosen because without toilets and clean water even the most resource-efficient, multi-faceted cultivation methods and nutritious diets are next to useless. The women share their newly-acquired knowledge and practices with surrounding villages.

The overall objective is Improved Household Food and Nutrition Security among vulnerable households in Kenema and Tonkolili district in Sierra Leone.The project aims to contribute to this objective through the following outcomes:Improved diversity and quality of the household diet, with a specific focus on women and young children, in targeted communities ;Enhanced ability of vulnerable Households to improve Food and Nutrition Security through sustainable use of natural resources; Improved hygiene and sanitation situation in the targeted communities leading to reduced prevalence of diarrhea; Inter-sectorial learning and coordination on Food and Nutrition Security enhanced at district and national level.

The project targets vulnerable households in remote communities in forested areas in Kenema and Tonkolili districts of Sierra Leone. The project is implemented primarily through 51 pre-existing women groups across 40 communities, in total 1403 women and their households, reaching around 11,645 people expected to benefit from improved nutrition, hygiene and agricultural practices. The project mobilizes direct beneficiaries to cascade nutrition messages and new agricultural technologies to additional groups and communities. These groups are defined together with the direct target group according to needs and vulnerability criteria discussed with them, but with a focus on improving nutrition and care for pregnant and lactating mothers and children under five.
